summary:
An AI-powered environmental early-warning dashboard integrates NASA Earth observation data with Sarawak’s unique topography to protect vulnerable communities along the Rajang River and rural Miri. The system is developed by fusing real-time NASA satellite feeds—including GPM rainfall tracking, SMAP soil moisture sensors, and cloud-penetrating radar—with high-resolution Digital Elevation Models of Sarawak’s steep interior highlands, meandering river basins, and coastal peatlands. Machine learning models trained on historical weather patterns and local river telemetry then forecast flood surges and landslides on an interactive map, sending automated alerts to emergency authorities and village leaders .
This integrated approach directly solves Sarawak’s severe environmental monitoring challenges. The Rajang and Baram basins span vast, isolated interiors where physical ground stations are sparse and persistent tropical cloud cover blocks standard optical satellites.Combining all-weather radar telemetry with local terrain modeling enables continuous tracking of rapid upstream runoff, coastal king-tide backflows, and hillside saturation.
